plan.title: Kidney treated vs control DE, batch-adjusted
plan.analytical_narrative:
The research question is a plain two-group differential expression: which genes differ between treated and control in 12 human kidney bulk RNA-seq samples (counts.csv, 12000 genes x 12 samples, salmon gene-level raw integer counts, gene symbols in the first column), with two known processing batches each holding both conditions (metadata.csv, 12 rows x 3 columns: sample, condition, batch). Because the batch is known and balanced across conditions, the batch belongs in the design formula as a fixed effect (~ batch + condition) and the counts must NOT be batch-corrected before the test — adjusting counts and then testing them reports confidence the data does not support. ComBat-seq or removeBatchEffect are permitted only to produce a visualisation matrix, never an input to the test.

Step T1S1 runs sample-structure QC before any model: blind VST, PCA on the 500 most variable genes coloured by condition and by batch, a sample-distance heatmap, and library sizes. With n=6 per group this is the step that reveals whether batch or condition dominates the primary variance axis and whether any of the 12 samples is an outlier; its findings condition how the T1S2 results are read. Step T1S2 is the test itself: minimal pre-filter (>=10 counts in >=6 samples, the smallest group size), median-of-ratios size factors estimated inside the model, DESeq2 Wald test on ~ batch + condition with the reference level of condition set explicitly to control so a positive log2 fold change means higher in treated, apeglm shrinkage of the reported fold change, BH adjustment at alpha 0.05 with independent filtering left on, and the p-value histogram inspected before the adjustment. Step T1S3 is the robustness cross-check and report: an edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test on the same filtered counts and the same design, the intersection with the DESeq2 calls reported as the high-confidence set (six replicates per group sits at the low end where the two tools disagree most), MA and dispersion diagnostics, and a full reproducibility record.

The question asks which genes differ — nothing more. No enrichment, deconvolution, or translational step is planned, because the user did not ask for pathways and 12 samples in one tissue would not support an unasked interpretive layer. Scope caveat: 12,000 genes is a pre-reduced matrix rather than a full transcriptome, so the tested universe is whatever that file contains, and the plan says so in the report rather than implying genome-wide coverage.
